records.source: וּכְהִתְפַּלֵּ֤ל עֶזְרָא֙ וּכְ֨הִתְוַדֹּת֔וֹבֹּכֶה֙ וּמִתְנַפֵּ֔ל לִפְנֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים נִקְבְּצוּ֩ אֵלָ֨יו מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֜ל קָהָ֣ל רַב־מְאֹ֗ד אֲנָשִׁ֤ים וְנָשִׁים֙ וִֽילָדִ֔ים כִּֽי־בָכ֥וּ הָעָ֖ם הַרְבֵּה־בֶֽכֶה׃ס
records.gloss: And as prayed Ezra and as he confessed, weeping and throwing himself down before [the] house of God, gathered to him from Israel an assembly great very, men and women and children, for wept the people [a] great weeping.
pieces: While Ezra was praying and confessing, weeping and throwing himself down before the house of God, a very large assembly of men, women, and children from Israel gathered around him, and the people wept bitterly.

L.1: And as Ezra prayed and as he confessed, weeping and throwing himself down before the house of God, a very great assembly gathered to him from Israel, men and women and children, for the people wept [with] much weeping.

R.1: Ezra was praying and confessing the people's sins. He was crying and lying face down in front of God's temple. While he did this, a very large crowd of Israelites gathered around him: men, women, and children. They were all crying hard.

decisions.choice: Ezra prayed: the account now speaks of Ezra as "he", not "I"
decisions.reason: From 7:27 to 9:15 Ezra tells his story in the first person. Chapter 10 goes on with the same events but calls him "Ezra" and "he", as the book did in 7:1-11. The change of voice does not change the events: the prayer of 9:6-15 is the prayer meant here.

decisions.choice: confessed, throwing himself down: confessing the people's sin while lying on the ground
decisions.reason: The verb for confess is the one used for confessing sin over the sacrifice on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:21) and in the prayers of Nehemiah 1:6 and 9:2-3. The second verb means to throw oneself down full length, as Moses did when he prayed for the people (Deuteronomy 9:18, 25).

decisions.choice: a very great assembly: a large gathering of the people
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for Israel gathered as a community. The crowd gathers of its own accord before the formal assembly of verses 7-9, and it includes women and children, whose families are at stake.

decisions.choice: lying face down; God's temple; a very large crowd (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable describes the posture, uses the book-wide wording for the house of God, and calls the gathering a crowd, since it has not yet been formally called together.

records.heading: A covenant to send away the foreign wives

records.source: וַיַּעַן֩ שְׁכַנְיָ֨ה בֶן־יְחִיאֵ֜ל מִבְּנֵ֤י עֵילָם֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְעֶזְרָ֔א אֲנַ֨חְנוּ֙ מָעַ֣לְנוּ בֵאלֹהֵ֔ינוּ וַנֹּ֛שֶׁב נָשִׁ֥ים נָכְרִיּ֖וֹת מֵעַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ וְעַתָּ֛ה יֵשׁ־מִקְוֶ֥ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַל־זֹֽאת׃
records.gloss: And answered Shecaniah son of Jehiel, of [the] sons of Elam, and said to Ezra, We, we have acted unfaithfully against our God, and we have settled women foreign from [the] peoples of the land; and now there is hope for Israel concerning this.
pieces: Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, one of the descendants of Elam, spoke up and said to Ezra, "We have been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign wives from the peoples of the land. But even so, there is still hope for Israel.

L.2: And Shecaniah son of Jehiel, of the sons of Elam, answered and said to Ezra, "We have been unfaithful to our God and have married foreign women from the peoples of the land, yet now there is hope for Israel concerning this.

R.2: Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, from the family of Elam, said to Ezra, "We have been unfaithful to our God. We married foreign wives from the people living in the land. But even now there is still hope for Israel.

decisions.choice: Elam: the reading the scribes marked
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text (ketiv) can be read "Olam"; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is "Elam", the family named in 2:7, 8:7 and 10:26. The two differ by one letter, and Elam is the name meant.

decisions.choice: Shecaniah son of Jehiel: perhaps the son of one of the offenders
decisions.reason: A Jehiel of the descendants of Elam is listed among the men who had married foreign wives (10:26). If he is Shecaniah's father, Shecaniah is proposing a step that will touch his own family. The name is common, so this is not certain.

decisions.choice: we have married foreign women: literally, we have settled foreign women (in our homes)
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause to dwell or give a home to. In this sense, for marrying, it is used only here and in Nehemiah 13:23, 27. The women are foreign in the sense of belonging to the other peoples of the land, not to the returned community.

decisions.choice: the sons of Elam (Literal), the descendants of Elam (Balanced), the family of Elam (Readable); foreign women (Literal), foreign wives (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: These follow the book-wide wording for family names in the lists and for the foreign wives.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה נִֽכְרָת־בְּרִ֣ית לֵ֠אלֹהֵינוּ לְהוֹצִ֨יא כָל־נָשִׁ֜ים וְהַנּוֹלָ֤ד מֵהֶם֙ בַּעֲצַ֣ת אֲדֹנָ֔י וְהַחֲרֵדִ֖ים בְּמִצְוַ֣ת אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְכַתּוֹרָ֖ה יֵעָשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: And now let us cut a covenant with our God to send out all [the] wives and the [one] born from them, by [the] counsel of [the] Lord and the trembling at [the] commandment of our God; and according to [the] law let it be done.
pieces: So now let us make a covenant with our God to send away all these wives and their children, following the counsel of the Lord and of those who tremble at the commandment of our God. Let it be done according to the law.

L.3: So now let us make a covenant with our God to send away all the wives and those born from them, according to the counsel of the Lord and of those who tremble at the commandment of our God; and let it be done according to the law.

R.3: Let us make a covenant with our God now. We will send away all these wives and their children. We will follow the advice of the Lord and of the people who take God's commands seriously. Let us do what the law says.

decisions.choice: let us cut a covenant: let us make a solemn binding agreement
decisions.reason: "Cutting" a covenant is the usual Hebrew way of saying it was made, perhaps from the animals cut in two when a covenant was sealed (Genesis 15:9-18; Jeremiah 34:18). The people bind themselves before God, as they do again in Nehemiah 10:1.

decisions.choice: send away the wives and those born from them: dissolve the marriages, with the children going with their mothers
decisions.reason: To send a wife out is to divorce her (compare Deuteronomy 24:1-2, which uses a related verb). "The wives" are the foreign wives of verse 2. The children go with their mothers, which was usual where a marriage ended.

decisions.choice: the counsel of the Lord, or of my lord
decisions.reason: The vowels of the received text read the word as "the Lord", that is, God. The same consonants can be read "my lord", a polite way of addressing Ezra; that reading fits the pairing with "those who tremble" and the "counsel of the leaders" in verse 8. The translation follows the vowels of the received text.

decisions.choice: according to the law: as the law of Moses requires
decisions.reason: The law forbade marriage with the peoples of the land (Deuteronomy 7:3) and set rules for sending a wife away (Deuteronomy 24:1-4). Shecaniah asks that what is done be done in line with the law, which Ezra had been sent to teach (7:10, 25).

decisions.choice: all these wives (Balanced, Readable); the people who take God's commands seriously (Readable)
decisions.reason: "These" makes clear that the foreign wives of verse 2 are meant, not all wives. Readable explains trembling at the commandment as in 9:4.

records.source: ק֛וּם כִּֽי־עָלֶ֥יךָ הַדָּבָ֖ר וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ עִמָּ֑ךְ חֲזַ֖ק וַעֲשֵֽׂה׃פ
records.gloss: Arise, for on you [is] the matter, and we [are] with you; be strong and act.
pieces: Get up, for this matter is your responsibility, and we are with you. Be strong and do it."

L.4: Arise, for the matter [is] on you, and we [are] with you; be strong and act."

R.4: Get up! It is your job to deal with this, and we will support you. Be brave and do it."

decisions.choice: the matter is on you: it is your responsibility
decisions.reason: Ezra had been sent by the king to teach the law and to appoint judges to enforce it (7:25-26), so the people look to him to act.

decisions.choice: be strong and act: words of encouragement for a hard task
decisions.reason: David spoke the same words to Solomon about building the temple (1 Chronicles 28:10, 20).

records.source: וַיָּ֣קָם עֶזְרָ֡א וַיַּשְׁבַּ֣ע אֶת־שָׂרֵי֩ הַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים הַלְוִיִּ֜ם וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לַעֲשׂ֛וֹת כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה וַיִּשָּׁבֵֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: And arose Ezra and made swear the princes of the priests, the Levites, and all Israel to do according to the word this; and they swore.
pieces: So Ezra got up and made the leading priests and Levites and all Israel take an oath to do what had been proposed. And they took the oath.

L.5: And Ezra arose and made the princes of the priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear to do according to this word; and they swore.

R.5: So Ezra got up. He made the leaders of the priests and the Levites and all the people of Israel promise with an oath to do what Shecaniah had said. And they made that promise.

decisions.choice: the princes of the priests, the Levites, and all Israel: the leaders of the three groups
decisions.reason: "The princes" most likely governs all three: the heads of the priests, of the Levites, and of the people. The oath binds the community through its leaders.

decisions.choice: made them swear: an oath taken in God's name
decisions.reason: An oath called on God as witness and judge of anyone who broke it (Nehemiah 10:30; 13:25). It gives the covenant Shecaniah proposed its binding force.

decisions.choice: what had been proposed (Balanced), what Shecaniah had said (Readable)
decisions.reason: "This word" points to Shecaniah's proposal in verses 2-4; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וַיָּ֣קָם עֶזְרָ֗א מִלִּפְנֵי֙ בֵּ֣ית הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ אֶל־לִשְׁכַּ֖ת יְהוֹחָנָ֣ן בֶּן־אֶלְיָשִׁ֑יב וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ שָׁ֗ם לֶ֤חֶם לֹֽא־אָכַל֙ וּמַ֣יִם לֹֽא־שָׁתָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִתְאַבֵּ֖ל עַל־מַ֥עַל הַגּוֹלָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And rose Ezra from before [the] house of God and went to [the] chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib; and he went there; bread not he ate and water not he drank, for he was mourning over the unfaithfulness of the exile.
pieces: Then Ezra left his place before the house of God and went to the room of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. He went there, but he ate no food and drank no water, because he was mourning over the unfaithfulness of the returned exiles.

L.6: And Ezra rose from before the house of God and went to the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib, and he went there; he ate no bread and drank no water, for he was mourning over the unfaithfulness of the exile.

R.6: Then Ezra left the front of God's temple and went to the room of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. While he was there, he did not eat any food or drink any water. He was mourning because the people who came back from exile had been unfaithful.

decisions.choice: and he went there: perhaps "and he spent the night there"
alternatives: and he spent the night there
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "he went", which reads awkwardly after "went to the chamber". The Greek book called 1 Esdras, which retells this chapter, has "spent the night there" (1 Esdras 9:2); in Hebrew the two verbs differ by one letter. The received text is translated, and the other reading is noted.

decisions.choice: the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib: a room in the temple buildings
decisions.reason: Rooms around the temple courts were used for storage and lodging (8:29; Nehemiah 13:4-9). A Johanan descended from the high priest Eliashib is named in Nehemiah 12:22-23; whether he is this Jehohanan is not certain, since both names were common.

decisions.choice: he ate no bread and drank no water: a complete fast in mourning
decisions.reason: Going without water as well as food is an extreme fast, like that of Moses when he pleaded for the people after the golden calf (Deuteronomy 9:18). Ezra mourns the people's sin as if for a death.

decisions.choice: chamber (Literal), room (Balanced, Readable); bread (Literal), food (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Bread" stands for food in general here.

records.source: וַיַּעֲבִ֨ירוּ ק֜וֹל בִּיהוּדָ֣ה וִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֗ם לְכֹל֙ בְּנֵ֣י הַגּוֹלָ֔ה לְהִקָּבֵ֖ץ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: And they made pass a proclamation in Judah and Jerusalem to all [the] sons of the exile to gather [to] Jerusalem;
pieces: A proclamation was sent throughout Judah and Jerusalem to all the returned exiles that they were to assemble in Jerusalem.

L.7: And they made a proclamation pass through Judah and Jerusalem to all the sons of the exile, to assemble [at] Jerusalem,

R.7: Then a message was sent all over Judah and Jerusalem to all the people who came back from exile. It told them to meet together in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Judah and Jerusalem: the small Persian province around Jerusalem
decisions.reason: In Ezra's time Judah was a small province of the Persian empire, with Jerusalem at its center, so a summons could reach every town within the three days set in verse 8.

decisions.choice: the sons of the exile: the returned exiles and their families
decisions.reason: The phrase names the community as a whole, those who had come back from Babylon and their descendants (4:1; 6:19-20).

decisions.choice: the sons of the exile (Literal), the returned exiles (Balanced), the people who came back from exile (Readable)
decisions.reason: These follow the book-wide wording for this phrase.

records.source: וְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־יָב֜וֹא לִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת הַיָּמִ֗ים כַּעֲצַ֤ת הַשָּׂרִים֙ וְהַזְּקֵנִ֔ים יָחֳרַ֖ם כָּל־רְכוּשׁ֑וֹ וְה֥וּא יִבָּדֵ֖ל מִקְּהַ֥ל הַגּוֹלָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: and everyone who not comes within three days, according to [the] counsel of the princes and the elders, shall be devoted all his property, and he shall be separated from [the] assembly of the exile.
pieces: Anyone who did not come within three days, as the leaders and elders had decided, would forfeit all his property and would himself be cut off from the assembly of the returned exiles.

L.8: and everyone who did not come within three days, according to the counsel of the princes and the elders, all his property would be devoted, and he himself would be separated from the assembly of the exile.

R.8: The leaders and elders decided that anyone who did not come within three days would lose everything he owned. His property would be given over to God, and he would no longer belong to the community of the people who came back from exile.

decisions.choice: all his property would be devoted: taken from him and given over to God
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for things devoted to God, which could never be bought back (Leviticus 27:28). Here it means the property would be confiscated, most likely for the temple. Artaxerxes had given Ezra power to punish by confiscating goods (7:26).

decisions.choice: separated from the assembly: excluded from the community
decisions.reason: The verb is the same as in 9:1 and 10:11, where the people are to separate themselves from the peoples of the land. Anyone who refused to come would himself be separated, put out of the community of the returned exiles.

decisions.choice: devoted (Literal), forfeit (Balanced), given over to God (Readable)
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the word is rendered "devoted" or "destroyed completely", but here the property is not destroyed. Balanced says what happens to the owner; Readable says where the property goes.

records.source: וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ כָל־אַנְשֵֽׁי־יְהוּדָה֩ וּבִנְיָמִ֨ן׀יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת הַיָּמִ֗ים ה֛וּא חֹ֥דֶשׁ הַתְּשִׁיעִ֖י בְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים בַּחֹ֑דֶשׁ וַיֵּשְׁב֣וּ כָל־הָעָ֗ם בִּרְחוֹב֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים מַרְעִידִ֥ים עַל־הַדָּבָ֖ר וּמֵהַגְּשָׁמִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: And assembled all [the] men of Judah and Benjamin [at] Jerusalem within three the days; it [was] the month the ninth, on [the] twentieth in the month; and sat all the people in [the] square of [the] house of God, trembling over the matter and from the rains.
pieces: So within the three days all the men of Judah and Benjamin assembled in Jerusalem. It was the twentieth day of the ninth month. All the people sat in the open square in front of the house of God, trembling because of this matter and because of the heavy rain.

L.9: And all the men of Judah and Benjamin assembled [at] Jerusalem within the three days; it [was] the ninth month, on the twentieth of the month. And all the people sat in the square of the house of God, trembling because of the matter and because of the rains.

R.9: So within three days all the men of Judah and Benjamin came together in Jerusalem. It was the twentieth day of the ninth month, in the rainy season of winter. All the people sat in the open square in front of God's temple. They were trembling because of this serious matter and shivering in the heavy rain.

decisions.choice: the twentieth day of the ninth month: in early winter, the rainy season
decisions.reason: The ninth month (Kislev) falls in November and December, when the winter rains come and it is cold in Jerusalem (Jeremiah 36:22). Ezra had arrived in the fifth month (7:9), so this is more than four months later.

decisions.choice: Judah and Benjamin: the tribes of the returned community
decisions.reason: Those who returned from exile came mostly from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin (1:5; 4:1).

decisions.choice: trembling because of the matter and the rains: fear and cold together
decisions.reason: The people tremble from fear over what they have done and what may follow, and from the cold rain falling on them as they sit in the open.

decisions.choice: in the rainy season of winter; trembling ... and shivering (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the season, which the month implies (verse 13), and uses two verbs for the one Hebrew word, since fear and cold are two different causes.

records.heading: The assembly in the rain at Jerusalem

records.source: וַיָּ֨קָם עֶזְרָ֤א הַכֹּהֵן֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אַתֶּ֣ם מְעַלְתֶּ֔ם וַתֹּשִׁ֖יבוּ נָשִׁ֣ים נָכְרִיּ֑וֹת לְהוֹסִ֖יף עַל־אַשְׁמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And arose Ezra the priest and said to them, You, you have acted unfaithfully and have settled women foreign, to add to [the] guilt of Israel.
pieces: Then Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, "You have been unfaithful by marrying foreign wives, and so you have added to Israel's guilt.

L.10: And Ezra the priest arose and said to them, "You have been unfaithful and have married foreign women, to add to the guilt of Israel.

R.10: Then Ezra the priest stood up and spoke to them. He said, "You have been unfaithful to God. You married foreign wives and made Israel even more guilty.

decisions.choice: to add to the guilt of Israel: the guilt already weighing on the people
decisions.reason: Ezra's prayer spoke of guilt piled up since the days of the ancestors (9:6-7, 13). The marriages add more to it.

decisions.choice: you have been unfaithful: the same word as in 9:2, 4 and 10:2
decisions.reason: The charge uses the key word of these chapters, a breach of trust against God.

decisions.choice: unfaithful to God (Readable)
decisions.reason: The unfaithfulness is against God (10:2); Readable says so.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה תְּנ֥וּ תוֹדָ֛ה לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֖ם וַעֲשׂ֣וּ רְצוֹנ֑וֹ וְהִבָּֽדְלוּ֙ מֵעַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ וּמִן־הַנָּשִׁ֖ים הַנָּכְרִיּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And now give confession to YHWH, [the] God of your fathers, and do his will, and separate yourselves from [the] peoples of the land and from the women foreign.
pieces: Now make confession to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, and do {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will. Separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from your foreign wives."

L.11: And now make confession to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, and do {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will, and separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign women."

R.11: Now confess your sin to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, and do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants. Separate yourselves from the people living in the land and from your foreign wives."

decisions.choice: give confession: acknowledge your sin before God
decisions.reason: The word often means thanks or praise, but with "give" it can mean to confess, giving God his due by admitting the wrong, as Joshua told Achan to do (Joshua 7:19).

decisions.choice: separate yourselves: the step the people had failed to take
decisions.reason: The leaders' complaint in 9:1 was that the people had not separated themselves from the peoples of the land. Ezra now calls on them to do it.

records.source: וַיַּֽעְנ֧וּ כָֽל־הַקָּהָ֛ל וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ ק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל כֵּ֛ן כִּדְבָרְךָ֥ עָלֵ֖ינוּ לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃
records.gloss: And answered all the assembly and said [with a] voice great, So! According to your word [it is] upon us to do.
pieces: The whole assembly answered with a loud voice, "Yes! We must do as you have said.

L.12: And all the assembly answered and said with a loud voice, "So [it is]! According to your word, [it is] upon us to do.

R.12: All the people answered with a loud voice, "Yes! You are right. We must do what you said.

decisions.choice: your word: the reading the scribes marked
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text (ketiv) read "your words"; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is "your word". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: upon us to do: it is our duty to do it
decisions.reason: "It is on us" means it is our responsibility, as "the matter is on you" did for Ezra in verse 4. The people accept the duty, then raise the practical difficulty in verse 13.

records.source: אֲבָ֞ל הָעָ֥ם רָב֙ וְהָעֵ֣ת גְּשָׁמִ֔ים וְאֵ֥ין כֹּ֖חַ לַעֲמ֣וֹד בַּח֑וּץ וְהַמְּלָאכָ֗ה לֹֽא־לְי֤וֹם אֶחָד֙ וְלֹ֣א לִשְׁנַ֔יִם כִּֽי־הִרְבִּ֥ינוּ לִפְשֹׁ֖עַ בַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: But the people [are] many, and the time [is] rains, and there is no strength to stand outside; and the work not for day one and not for two, for we have multiplied to transgress in the matter this.
pieces: But there are many people here, and it is the rainy season; we cannot stand out in the open. Besides, this is not a task for one or two days, because many of us have sinned seriously in this matter.

L.13: But the people [are] many, and it [is] the season of rains, and there is no strength to stand outside; and the work [is] not for one day or for two, for we have greatly transgressed in this matter.

R.13: But there are so many people, and it is the rainy season. We cannot keep standing out here in the rain. And this cannot be done in one or two days, because so many of us have sinned in this way.

decisions.choice: we have multiplied to transgress: many of us have sinned, and the sin is great
decisions.reason: The verb "multiply" with "to transgress" can mean that the sin was great, or that many committed it. The reason given (the work will take more than a day or two) points to the number of cases; both are true.

decisions.choice: transgress: rebel, break faith
decisions.reason: The verb means to rebel against an authority or to break an agreement. It is a strong word for sin, set beside "unfaithfulness" in verse 10.

decisions.choice: greatly transgressed (Literal), many of us have sinned seriously (Balanced), so many of us have sinned (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps both senses of the verb; Readable gives the one that explains why the work will take long.

records.source: יַֽעֲמְדוּ־נָ֣א שָׂ֠רֵינוּ לְֽכָל־הַקָּהָ֞ל וְכֹ֣ל׀אֲשֶׁ֣ר בֶּעָרֵ֗ינוּ הַהֹשִׁ֞יב נָשִׁ֤ים נָכְרִיּוֹת֙ יָבֹא֙ לְעִתִּ֣ים מְזֻמָּנִ֔ים וְעִמָּהֶ֛ם זִקְנֵי־עִ֥יר וָעִ֖יר וְשֹׁפְטֶ֑יהָ עַ֠ד לְהָשִׁ֞יב חֲר֤וֹן אַף־אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ עַ֖ד לַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃פ
records.gloss: Let stand please our princes for all the assembly, and all who [are] in our cities who has settled women foreign, let him come at times appointed, and with them [the] elders of city and city and its judges, until turning back [the] burning of [the] anger of our God from us, until for the matter this.
pieces: Let our leaders act for the whole assembly. Let everyone in our towns who has married a foreign wife come at a set time, together with the elders and judges of each town, until the fierce anger of our God over this matter is turned away from us."

L.14: Let our princes stand for the whole assembly, and let all who are in our cities who have married foreign women come at appointed times, and with them the elders and judges of each city, until the burning anger of our God is turned back from us over this matter."

R.14: Let our leaders act for all the people here. Then let every man in our towns who has married a foreign wife come at a time that is set for him. The elders and judges of his town should come with him. We must do this until our God is no longer angry with us about this."

decisions.choice: let our princes stand for the whole assembly: let the leaders act on behalf of everyone
decisions.reason: Instead of the whole people standing in the rain, the leaders are to represent them and oversee the cases.

decisions.choice: the elders of city and city and its judges: the elders and judges of each town
decisions.reason: Repeating a noun means "each". The local elders and judges knew the families and could confirm the facts of each case, as Ezra had been told to appoint judges (7:25).

decisions.choice: the burning of the anger of our God: God's fierce anger
decisions.reason: "Burning of anger" is a strong phrase for wrath (Numbers 25:4; 2 Chronicles 29:10). The leaders fear what Ezra feared in 9:14.

decisions.choice: until, concerning this matter: the last words are compressed
alternatives: until this matter is dealt with
decisions.reason: The Hebrew ends with "until for this matter", which most likely ties God's anger to this matter ("over this matter"). It can also be read as a second time limit, "until this matter is settled". Either way the sense of the plan is clear.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal), leaders (Balanced, Readable); towns (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 9:1-2. The places meant are the towns and villages of Judah, so Balanced and Readable say "towns".

records.source: אַ֣ךְ יוֹנָתָ֧ן בֶּן־עֲשָׂהאֵ֛ל וְיַחְזְיָ֥ה בֶן־תִּקְוָ֖ה עָמְד֣וּ עַל־זֹ֑את וּמְשֻׁלָּ֛ם וְשַׁבְּתַ֥י הַלֵּוִ֖י עֲזָרֻֽם׃
records.gloss: Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah stood against this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them.
pieces: Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah opposed this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supported them.

L.15: Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah stood against this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supported them.

R.15: Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah were against this plan, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite took their side.

decisions.choice: stood against this: opposed the plan
decisions.reason: "Stood against" usually means to oppose (Daniel 8:25; 11:14), and "only" fits a small group who disagreed. The words can also mean "stood over this", that is, were put in charge of it, and some have read it that way. The text does not say why they objected, or whether to the plan itself or to the delay.

decisions.choice: supported them: helped them, took their side
decisions.reason: The verb means to help. If the first two men opposed the plan, Meshullam and Shabbethai backed their objection.

records.source: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵן֮ בְּנֵ֣י הַגּוֹלָה֒ וַיִּבָּדְלוּ֩ עֶזְרָ֨א הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֲנָשִׁ֨ים רָאשֵׁ֧י הָאָב֛וֹת לְבֵ֥ית אֲבֹתָ֖ם וְכֻלָּ֣ם בְּשֵׁמ֑וֹת וַיֵּשְׁב֗וּ בְּי֤וֹם אֶחָד֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִ֔י לְדַרְי֖וֹשׁ הַדָּבָֽר׃
records.gloss: And did so [the] sons of the exile; and were set apart Ezra the priest, men, heads of the fathers, for [the] house of their fathers, and all of them by names; and they sat on day one of the month the tenth to examine the matter.
pieces: So the returned exiles did as they had proposed. Ezra the priest and certain heads of families, one for each family and all of them named, were set apart for the task. On the first day of the tenth month they sat down to investigate the matter.

L.16: And the sons of the exile did so. And Ezra the priest [and] men, heads of the fathers, by their fathers' houses, all of them by name, were set apart; and they sat down on the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter.

R.16: So the people who came back from exile did what had been planned. Ezra the priest and some heads of families were chosen for this work, one for each family, and each one was named. On the first day of the tenth month they sat down to look into each case.

decisions.choice: were set apart, Ezra ... men: perhaps "Ezra set apart for himself men"
alternatives: Ezra the priest set apart men who were heads of families
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads awkwardly: a plural passive verb with "Ezra the priest, men, heads of families". 1 Esdras 9:16 has "Ezra chose for himself men", which a small change in the Hebrew letters would also give. Either way Ezra and the family heads together form the panel that hears the cases.

decisions.choice: to examine: to investigate each case
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek or inquire, here in the sense of a careful inquiry. It is spelled in an unusual way that looks like the name Darius; the meaning is not in doubt.

decisions.choice: the first day of the tenth month: ten days after the assembly
decisions.reason: The assembly met on the twentieth day of the ninth month (verse 9), so the panel began its work ten days later, in midwinter.

decisions.choice: heads of the fathers, fathers' houses (Literal); heads of families, family (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: These follow the wording used for the ancestral family across the Old Testament books.

records.source: וַיְכַלּ֣וּ בַכֹּ֔ל אֲנָשִׁ֕ים הַהֹשִׁ֖יבוּ נָשִׁ֣ים נָכְרִיּ֑וֹת עַ֛ד י֥וֹם אֶחָ֖ד לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃פ
records.gloss: And they finished with all, [the] men who had settled women foreign, by day one of the month the first.
pieces: By the first day of the first month they had finished dealing with all the men who had married foreign wives.

L.17: And they finished with all the men who had married foreign women by the first day of the first month.

R.17: By the first day of the first month of the next year, they had finished with all the cases of men who had married foreign wives.

decisions.choice: the first day of the first month: three months later, a year after Ezra set out
decisions.reason: The inquiry ran from the first day of the tenth month to the first day of the first month of the next year. Ezra had left Babylon on the first day of the first month (7:9), so the work ends a year to the day after his journey began.

decisions.choice: they finished with all: they completed their inquiry into every case
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "with all, the men", meaning everything concerning the men. It says that the inquiry was completed; what followed for each household is told only in verses 19 and 44.

decisions.choice: of the next year (Readable)
decisions.reason: The first month comes after the tenth, so it belongs to the following year; Readable says so.

records.source: וַיִּמָּצֵא֙ מִבְּנֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֹשִׁ֖יבוּ נָשִׁ֣ים נָכְרִיּ֑וֹת מִבְּנֵ֨ייֵשׁ֤וּעַ בֶּן־יֽוֹצָדָק֙ וְאֶחָ֔יו מַֽעֲשֵׂיָה֙ וֶֽאֱלִיעֶ֔זֶר וְיָרִ֖יב וּגְדַלְיָֽה׃
records.gloss: And was found of [the] sons of the priests who had settled women foreign: of [the] sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers, Maaseiah and Eliezer and Jarib and Gedaliah.
pieces: These were found to have married foreign wives. From the priests: of the descendants of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers, Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.

L.18: And there were found among the sons of the priests [some] who had married foreign women: of the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers, Maaseiah and Eliezer and Jarib and Gedaliah.

R.18: These are the men who were found to have married foreign wives. From the priests' families, from the family of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his relatives, there were Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.

decisions.choice: the list begins with the priests, and with the high priest's own family
decisions.reason: Jeshua son of Jozadak was the high priest who led the first return with Zerubbabel and rebuilt the altar (3:2; 5:2; Haggai 1:1). His descendants head the list, which then runs through the priests, the Levites, the singers and gatekeepers, and the people, in the order of the list of returned exiles in chapter 2.

decisions.choice: his brothers: his relatives, his fellow priests
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means the kinsmen of Jeshua's house, not only his brothers by birth.

decisions.choice: the sons of (Literal), the descendants of (Balanced), the family of (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for family names in the lists, used through verse 43.

records.heading: Those found to have married foreign wives

records.source: וַיִּתְּנ֥וּ יָדָ֖ם לְהוֹצִ֣יא נְשֵׁיהֶ֑ם וַאֲשֵׁמִ֥ים אֵֽיל־צֹ֖אן עַל־אַשְׁמָתָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And they gave their hand to send out their wives, and guilty, a ram of [the] flock for their guilt.
pieces: They pledged themselves to send away their wives, and because they were guilty they offered a ram from the flock as a guilt offering.

L.19: And they gave their hand to send away their wives, and [being] guilty, [they offered] a ram of the flock for their guilt.

R.19: They promised to send away their wives. Because they were guilty, they brought a ram from the flock as an offering to take away their guilt.

decisions.choice: they gave their hand: they pledged themselves
decisions.reason: Giving the hand was the gesture of a binding promise (2 Kings 10:15; 1 Chronicles 29:24).

decisions.choice: a ram for their guilt: the guilt offering the law required for unfaithfulness
decisions.reason: The law required a ram as a guilt offering from one who had been unfaithful in what belonged to God (Leviticus 5:14-19). The word for unfaithfulness there is the one used in 9:2 and 10:2.

decisions.choice: and guilty, a ram: a short phrase with no verb
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is compressed: "and guilty, a ram of the flock for their guilt". The verb "offered" is understood. It most likely applies to the priests just named; whether the others did the same is not said.

decisions.choice: [they offered] (Literal), they offered, they brought (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb is supplied to make an English sentence.

records.source: וּמִבְּנֵ֣י אִמֵּ֔ר חֲנָ֖נִי וּזְבַדְיָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And of [the] sons of Immer, Hanani and Zebadiah.
pieces: From the descendants of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.

L.20: And of the sons of Immer, Hanani and Zebadiah.

R.20: From the family of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.

decisions.choice: Immer, Harim, Pashhur: the other priestly families of the return
decisions.reason: The list of returned exiles names four priestly families: Jedaiah of the house of Jeshua, Immer, Pashhur and Harim (2:36-39). All four appear here (verses 18-22).

records.source: וּמִבְּנֵ֖י חָרִ֑ם מַעֲשֵׂיָ֤ה וְאֵֽלִיָּה֙ וּֽשְׁמַֽעְיָ֔ה וִיחִיאֵ֖ל וְעֻזִיָּֽה׃

R.21: From the family of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.

decisions.choice: Harim: a priestly family
decisions.reason: Harim is one of the priestly families of 2:39. A lay family of the same name follows in verse 31 (compare 2:32).

records.gloss: And of [the] sons of Pashhur, Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Eleasah.
pieces: From the descendants of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Eleasah.

L.22: And of the sons of Pashhur, Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Eleasah.

R.22: From the family of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Eleasah.

decisions.choice: Pashhur: the largest priestly family of the return
decisions.reason: Pashhur's descendants numbered 1,247 in the list of 2:38. With this verse the priests in the list number seventeen.

records.source: וּמִֽן־הַלְוִיִּ֑ם יוֹזָבָ֣ד וְשִׁמְעִ֗י וְקֵֽלָיָה֙ ה֣וּא קְלִיטָ֔א פְּתַֽחְיָ֥ה יְהוּדָ֖ה וֶאֱלִיעֶֽזֶר׃ס
records.gloss: And of the Levites: Jozabad and Shimei and Kelaiah, he [is] Kelita, Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
pieces: From the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.

L.23: And of the Levites: Jozabad and Shimei and Kelaiah, that [is] Kelita, Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.

R.23: From the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (also called Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.

decisions.choice: Kelaiah, that is, Kelita: one man known by two names
decisions.reason: A Levite named Kelita helps explain the law when Ezra reads it (Nehemiah 8:7) and signs the covenant (Nehemiah 10:11); the note here may identify him with this Kelaiah.

records.source: וּמִן־הַמְשֹׁרְרִ֖ים אֶלְיָשִׁ֑יב וּמִן־הַשֹּׁ֣עֲרִ֔ים שַׁלֻּ֥ם וָטֶ֖לֶם וְאוּרִֽי׃ס
records.gloss: And of the singers: Eliashib; and of the gatekeepers: Shallum and Telem and Uri.
pieces: From the singers: Eliashib. From the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.

L.24: And of the singers, Eliashib; and of the gatekeepers, Shallum and Telem and Uri.

R.24: From the temple singers: Eliashib. From the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.

decisions.choice: the singers and the gatekeepers: groups of temple servants
decisions.reason: The singers and the gatekeepers who guarded the temple gates are listed after the Levites in 2:41-42, and the same order is kept here.

records.source: וּמִֽיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִבְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֡שׁ רַ֠מְיָה וְיִזִּיָּ֤ה וּמַלְכִּיָּה֙ וּמִיָּמִ֣ן וְאֶלְעָזָ֔ר וּמַלְכִּיָּ֖ה וּבְנָיָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And of Israel: of [the] sons of Parosh, Ramiah and Izziah and Malkijah and Mijamin and Eleazar and Malkijah and Benaiah.
pieces: From the rest of Israel: from the descendants of Parosh, Ramiah, Izziah, Malkijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malkijah, and Benaiah.

L.25: And of Israel: of the sons of Parosh, Ramiah and Izziah and Malkijah and Mijamin and Eleazar and Malkijah and Benaiah.

R.25: From the other Israelites, from the family of Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malkijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malkijah, and Benaiah.

decisions.choice: of Israel: the laypeople, as distinct from priests and Levites
decisions.reason: "Israel" here means the people who were not priests, Levites or temple servants, as in 2:70 and 7:7. Their families follow roughly in the order of 2:3-20, beginning with Parosh.

decisions.choice: the rest of Israel (Balanced), the other Israelites (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that these are the remaining Israelites, since the priests and Levites were Israelites too.

records.source: וּמִבְּנֵ֖י עֵילָ֑ם מַתַּנְיָ֤ה זְכַרְיָה֙ וִיחִיאֵ֣ל וְעַבְדִּ֔י וִירֵמ֖וֹת וְאֵלִיָּֽה׃ס

pieces: From the descendants of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.

L.26: And of the sons of Elam, Mattaniah, Zechariah, and Jehiel and Abdi and Jeremoth and Elijah.

R.26: From the family of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.

decisions.choice: Elam, Jehiel: the family of Shecaniah
decisions.reason: Shecaniah, who proposed the covenant, was "son of Jehiel, of the descendants of Elam" (10:2). This Jehiel may be his father, though the name is common.

records.gloss: And of [the] sons of Zattu, Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, and Jeremoth and Zabad and Aziza.
pieces: From the descendants of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.

L.27: And of the sons of Zattu, Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, and Jeremoth and Zabad and Aziza.

R.27: From the family of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.

decisions.choice: Zattu: one of the large families of the first return
decisions.reason: The descendants of Zattu numbered 945 in the list of 2:8. Several names here (Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah) also occur in other families; such names were common.

L.28: And of the sons of Bebai, Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, Athlai.

R.28: From the family of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.

decisions.choice: Bebai: a family of the return
decisions.reason: Bebai's descendants appear in 2:11 and again among those who came with Ezra (8:11).

records.source: וּמִבְּנֵ֖י בָּנִ֑י מְשֻׁלָּ֤ם מַלּוּךְ֙ וַעֲדָיָ֔ה יָשׁ֖וּב וּשְׁאָ֥ל וְרָמֽוֹת׃ס

records.gloss: All these had taken women foreign, and there were of them women, and they had set sons.
pieces: All these had married foreign women, and some of them had wives by whom they had {{gender:children|sons}}.

L.44: All these had taken foreign women, and there were among them women [by whom] they had had sons.

R.44: All these men had married foreign women, and some of them had even had {{gender:children|sons}} with them.

decisions.choice: they had taken: the reading the scribes marked
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text (ketiv) give an unusual form of the verb; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is the ordinary "they had taken". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: some had wives by whom they had children: the last clause is difficult
alternatives: and they sent them away with their children (1 Esdras 9:36)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads, word for word, "and there were among them women, and they had set sons", which does not give a smooth sense; the verb "set" is not used elsewhere for having children. The translation takes it to mean that some of the marriages had produced children. The Greek retelling in 1 Esdras 9:36 ends instead "and they sent them away with their children", which may reflect a different Hebrew text. The received text is translated, and the other reading is noted.

decisions.choice: the book ends with the list
decisions.reason: The book of Ezra ends here, with the names of some 110 men and no account of what became of their households. The list holds the community's leaders and priests to account by name. The same problem returns a generation later (Nehemiah 13:23-27).

decisions.choice: children or sons (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for sons is also the ordinary word for children, and the families surely had daughters too, so Balanced and Readable offer "children" as the default. Literal keeps "sons".
